newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down, seen drifting lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down, seen drifting lower.

text.p: Rubber futures closed lower on Thursday in trade deadened by the Japanese holiday with the market seen drifting lower ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
"It was dead boring, but the mood couldn't be helped since the Japanese were out on a holiday. All the players in the market just fell asleep," a local rubber trader said.
Volume was extremely light while prices drifted lazily in the market, dealers said.
"The mood is going to probably be the same tomorrow with the weekend coming up," another dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, November RSS3 was seen at 123.00 U.S. cents a kg from 123.75 cents.
November RSS1 was seen at 175.25-176.25 Singapore cents (US$1.24-$1.25) a kg from Wednesday's settlement of 176.25 cents.
December TSR20 was seen at 173.00-174.00 Singapore cents (US$1.22-$1.23) a kg against the previous 174.25 cents.
